title: Design and implement hybrid SSE multiplexing + resumable delta envelope for streaming API
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: Our existing SSE streaming surface handles long-lived generation streams but lacks a compact multiplexing envelope and a robust resume protocol that works across legacy HTTP/1.1 clients and newer HTTP/2/3 transports. This results in (a) difficulty delivering multiple logical channels (e.g., tool calls + model tokens) on a single connection, (b) poor reconnection semantics when clients drop mid-generation, and (c) ambiguous behavior for structured outputs and function/tool call boundaries during reconnect.

Goal: Define and ship a hybrid SSE envelope format and server-side resume strategy that: (1) enables multiplexing of logical substreams over a single SSE connection, (2) provides compact resumable delta checkpoints so clients can rejoin mid-stream with minimal repetition, (3) preserves strong compatibility with existing clients that expect plain SSE or chunked HTTP responses, and (4) embeds explicit semantics for function/tool-call events and structured outputs so downstream SDKs can reliably rehydrate state after reconnects.
acceptance_criteria: Define an SSE 'envelope' event format that includes substream_id, sequence numbers, and optional resume_token in a single-line JSON data payload
Server exposes a resume endpoint or reconnection flow where clients can present last-seen resume_token + per-substream seq to receive missing deltas only
Fallback mode: if client cannot parse envelope JSON, server falls back to legacy newline-delimited chunks (back-compat), documented in API compatibility matrix
Function call events are emitted as dedicated substreams (e.g., substream 'tools') with clear open/close markers so SDKs can synthesize idempotent invocations on reconnect
Automated unit + integration tests demonstrating reconnect with partial KV cache and correct reassembly for multiplexed streams
Performance benchmarks showing <5% p99 latency regression for short streams and measured reduction in token duplication on reconnects compared to baseline
decision_log: 2026-02-26: Chose a JSON-envelope approach rather than custom binary framing — improves human debuggability and reduces SDK parsing complexity.
2026-03-01: Use base64 payloads only for binary tool attachments; otherwise send compact JSON with escaped strings to keep lines short for SSE.
2026-03-04: Multiplexing model: allocate logical substream ids (strings) per session; server maintains per-substream sequence counters and per-session resume_token which is a monotonic opaque cursor.

2026-03-06: Resume semantics: client must supply (resume_token, last_seq_by_substream) — server reconciles and streams missing deltas; if resume_token expired or mismatch, server falls back to full-stream reissue with explicit 'replay-start' marker.
2026-03-10: Backoff policy: clients should use jittered exponential backoff starting at 300ms, capped at 30s. Server can include Retry-After hints in a 'session-hint' SSE event.

2026-03-11: Compatibility: Support three modes - 'envelope' (modern), 'ndjson' (SDK-friendly), and 'legacy-chunked' (HTTP/1.1 proxies). Server selects mode based on Accept header + /connect parameter.
implementation_notes: SSE envelope schema (single-line JSON in event:data): {"t":"chunk","sub":"tokens","seq":123,"tok_count":8,"resume":"r_8f7b","payload":{...}}
Reserved substream ids: 'tokens', 'tools', 'meta', 'diagnostics'. Each substream has independent seq integers starting at 1 for the session.

Tool/function calling: emit a 'tools' substream event with payload: {"call_id":"c-uuid", "status":"invoked|result|error", "body":{...}}. On reconnect, SDK uses call_id + idempotency policy to avoid double-execution.
Resume_token generation: server creates opaque resume tokens bound to session id, minimal TTL configurable (default 5 minutes). Tokens are HMAC-signed to detect tampering.
Server-side retention: keep per-session delta buffers for resume TTL + small GC window to reduce storage. If client requests resume outside TTL, reply with 'replay-required' and full reissue.
Proxy considerations: some HTTP proxies discard SSE comment lines; avoid starting lines with colon-only comments; use explicit 'meta' events instead.
Fallbacks: when streaming over HTTP/1.1 without SSE support, provide 'X-Stream-Mode: ndjson' which emits newline-delimited envelope JSONs. This helps old SDKs parse without SSE parsing.
Headers and hints: include 'X-Stream-Version: 2' and 'X-Resume-Support: true' in initial response. Provide Link header to resume endpoint: <https://api.redwood.example/sessions/{id}/resume>
testing_plan: Unit tests for envelope encoder/decoder with malformed input and large payloads
Integration test harness simulating flaky connections (random disconnects) validating resume correctness across substreams
Compatibility test matrix: curl (HTTP/1.1), node-fetch (HTTP/2), browser SSE, and legacy proxy behavior
Load test: 10k concurrent SSE connections with mixed small/large streams to validate memory retention and GC behavior
Chaos test: server-side resume_token rotation + client reconnect to validate graceful 'replay-required' path
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable envelope mode behind feature flag for 5% of hosted traffic; monitor token duplication and error rates
Phase 2 (beta): SDKs (JS/Python/Go) published with automatic resume helper; invite top customers to opt-in
Phase 3: enable 'X-Stream-Mode: ndjson' fallback for older clients and update docs; run migration notes in console > streaming settings
Phase 4: full rollout with runtime-1.24 and deprecation notice for legacy-chunked mode after 90 days
notes_and_feedback: 2026-03-03 (PR review - @Anika Rao): Ensure resume tokens are short-lived; requested adding audit log entries for resume attempts.
2026-03-07 (Design - @Carlos B.): Suggested a compact tag set for tool events to reduce repeated keys in high-throughput flows.
2026-03-09 (Security - @Priya Singh): Requires threat model review for resume token replay; suggested binding token to client IP or TLS session as optional flag.
